prs.title: Prove smooth cusp population bars and fold-edge dominance
prs.head: f02758555b4bce4554e34e8913947f69578d0816
prs.body:
This construction proves the actual finite H0 barcode for a smooth two-control cusp population, then derives its lifetime density and marked independent-copy limit. Across the full control rectangle, almost every field has zero or one finite bar. Short bars approaching the ordinary fold edges give leading density C_edge * ell^(-1/3); controls restricted away from those edges give the smaller quartic-tip density C_tip * ell^(1/4). The comparison shows that the contact stratum and its sampling weight both belong in the universality taxonomy.

The proof reuses the explicit torus surgery from #336, derives uniform root, annular and height guards for the whole rectangle, and exhausts the global critical list. These guards identify the younger maximum and middle saddle as the actual elder merger. The total probability of a finite bar is at most 1/5. An integrable all-control bound handles the degenerating u→0 boundary and yields the leading cumulative count (3/2) * C_edge * t^(2/3). The away-edge tip formula is exact below its stated cutoff, with cumulative count (4/5) * C_tip * t^(5/4).

For independent whole copies with t_n→0 and n*t_n^(2/3)→lambda, the zero-or-one bar structure gives the stated Poisson random measure. Its latent control, sign and Haar-location marks are explicit; physical birth and cubic marks retain their shared-control correlation. This is one declared stationary non-Gaussian law. It supplies no general A3 classification, Gaussian contact admission, higher-homology theorem, same-field spatial limit, numerical/count coupling, compiler result or blind experiment.

prs.title: Prove stationary quartic H0 law with explicit sampling weights
prs.head: 3ab12c6542c88554ad0d42e0e19aff2461dc3c0d
prs.body:
A quartic contact does not assign a lifetime exponent without its sampling law. This adds an explicit smooth torus field with a complete critical-point list and exactly one globally selected finite superlevel H0 bar. A matched quartic surgery, protected annulus and fixed high-level enclosure prove that the younger maximum dies at the middle saddle; its lifetime is exactly C*lambda^2. Haar translation makes the field stationary.

A parameter density gamma*lambda^(gamma-1) on its declared finite interval gives exact lifetime density beta*ell0^(-beta)*ell^(beta-1), beta=gamma/2. Flat parameter density therefore realizes density power -1/2, while gamma=4/3 realizes -1/3 at the same quartic germ. The independent-whole-copy marked Poisson limit follows from an exact one-point Laplace calculation under t_n→0 and n*t_n^beta→Lambda. The physical separation and birth marks are derived separately. This restricted path is C1 but not C2 in its control at zero; the finite-dimensional two-site observation law is singular. No generic two-control cusp, Gaussian contact law or covariance match is claimed.

prs.head: 6bd133d591e43e75a9292463bb4bfde7a34984dc
prs.body:
Covariance and realization-wise Morse pairings do not determine the small-lifetime law. This adds an actual stationary field F=A H, where H is an admitted Gaussian spectral field, R has density alpha*r^(alpha-1) on(0,1), A=sqrt((alpha+2)/alpha)*R and E[A^2]=1. The field has exactly H's covariance and actual barcode pairings; every lifetime scales by A. It retains H's positive smooth-norm moments while its near-zero amplitude changes the population.

The exact density/cumulative transforms prove three leading regimes with beta=2/3: alpha<beta gives density power alpha-1 with a global barcode Mellin coefficient; alpha=beta gives t^(-1/3)*log(1/t); alpha>beta restores t^(-1/3) with multiplier E[A^(-2/3)]>1. Per-volume and whole-volume constants remain explicit. A lower-order unbounded far density can persist even when the leading fold power returns, so the literal Gaussian FAR contract is not inferred.

The independent-whole-copy process is also derived from its exact Laplace transform. Below beta it retains complete base barcodes as Poisson clusters; the full positive K5 base family supplies actual positive multi-bar probability and a strict void-rate falsifier for H0/all degrees. At the critical normalization t_n->0 and n*t_n^(2/3)*log(1/t_n)->lambda, the limit is an ordinary projected PRM with an optional uniform latent log-amplitude mark; physical birth/gap marks collapse. Above beta, n*t_n^(2/3)->lambda yields the ordinary marked PRM with the A^(-2/3)-tilted physical mark law. No within-one-field/spatial limit or factorial theorem is inferred.

prs.title: Extend regular-fold short bars to Hp and degree-marked iid limits
prs.head: 89657c7c48289378949dc59e7fbe6dc1a55d9c62
prs.body:
An isolated regular cubic fold now produces an actual ordinary Hp interval under the stated same-field C4 continuation and complete critical-list hypotheses. If the nonsingular transverse Hessian has j negative eigenvalues, the two superlevel handle degrees are p=d-j-1 and p+1. Exact transverse splitting gives one transverse adapted-flow connection. Crossing a fixed annulus would cost a positive height increment, while the available gap is k*r^3; additional global connecting orbits are excluded. The relative handle boundary coefficient is therefore a unit. With no intervening critical value, that unit forces the new class to be born and die at those exact two critical points.

The proof bridges the classical smooth incidence formula to the actual C4 filtration by fixed-r smooth approximation, aligned critical values and one regular-level isotopy preserving all sampled sublevels and inclusions. It constructs Borel once-counted finite-bar selectors. Zero-incidence CW/graph examples remain explicit failures of weaker adjacent-index assumptions, rather than purported realizations of this isolated fold.

Under the exact fixed stationary Gaussian SG carrier/rank/moment contracts, it proves canonical finite Borel densities nu_p(ell)~c_(q,p)*ell^(-1/3) as ell tends to zero for p=0,...,d-1, and cumulative mean per volume ~(3/2)c_(q,p)*t^(2/3). The coefficient is the actual law-specific jet functional with the index-(d-p-1) transverse inertia cone and universal factor Gamma(7/6)/(24^(1/3)*sqrt(pi)). Centered Gaussian cone symmetry gives c_(q,p)=c_(q,d-1-p). Unit incidence makes the leading coefficients independent of the chosen coefficient field; entire global barcodes need not be.

The new all-degree endpoint-exhaustion argument proves E[N_all(Tt);N_all(Tt)>=2]=o(t^(2/3)). It yields a degree-marked Poisson limit for independent whole copies with n*t^(2/3)->lambda>0. It does not claim a same-field spatial/expanding-domain limit, a second factorial or K7 estimate, numerical Hp computation/count coupling, torsion/integral interval persistence, arbitrary non-Gaussian/manifold probabilistic admission or critical Lean closure. Density continuity and a bounded near remainder are not asserted.

prs.head: 88ff9223e57bf38c7fc33cb3559a88793a7b5087
prs.body:
This proves actual short H0-bar asymptotics and an independent-whole-copy marked process limit for a reusable class of fixed stationary Gaussian spectral laws on the flat torus. A positive finite carrier supplies the named contact and off-contact ranks; actual C4 paths and norm moments supply the conditional continuation and domination. A simple sufficient condition is full positivity on |n|infinity<=5 and sum sqrt(q_n)(1+|2pi n/L|)^4<infinity. The law keeps its actual spectral weights, including its independent tail, and the coefficient uses its own jet covariance and conditional transverse Hessian.

The extensions include zero-mode removal with explicit rank witnesses, finite carriers with support holes, anisotropic unimodular shears, and polynomial spectral tails with beta>d+8 that satisfy the C4 moment route even when the stronger square-root summability condition fails. Degenerating covariance examples show why fixed-law admission does not give a uniform coefficient or physical window over arbitrary families. No covariance-matched non-Gaussian admission is inferred.

The topological population consists of actual global finite H0 intervals. The physical estimate E[N_(Tt); N_(Tt)>=2]=o(t^(2/3)) yields the iid whole-field rare-event process when n*t^(2/3)->lambda>0. Same-field spatial and expanding-domain limits, K7/coalescing-contact factorial estimates, higher homology, numerical sampler/count coupling, blind validation and critical Lean closure remain open for this PR.

This retains all supported ordinary/leading-zero major-1 forms, refuses zero or other major with the existing `ContractError('unsupported schema major')`, and does not parse/limit minor digits.
- Five additive `unittest` methods cover >5,000-digit unsupported versions, semantically major-1 padded versions, all five published example/validator routes, ordinary grammar and existing rejection messages.

- **Original isolated reproduction (CPython 3.13.5, default 4,300-digit conversion cap):** the exact original `parse_major` function body with `int(m.group(1))` raised raw `ValueError` for `'9'*5000+'.0'` and `'0'*5000+'1.0'`, whereas `'01.0'` returned 1. - **Candidate isolated-function controls (same interpreter):** 5,000-digit unsupported majors raise `ContractError`, padded semantic major 1 returns 1, ordinary 1 and 01 accepted, invalid grammar rejected. This is **not a full repository execution**.

C160's docs-only candidate main#293 exposed two failures in unchanged `tests/test_site_asset_release.py` at main `1653fe6740e9e2c8d36a47101bf7bb50c7aae273`, Python3.12.14 on macOS15.7.4. Both normal and optimized full410-method runs fail the same two tests with the default temporary directory:
